display.purpose: Identity moments only: logo monogram, H1/H2 section titles.

body.purpose: Everything else: paragraphs, labels, nav, buttons, badges, captions.

shadows.name: glow-on-response
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system; appears solely on primary-button hover and skip-link focus, never at rest.

motion.name: reveal-fade-up
motion.value: animate.css fadeInUp, 0.8s, triggered by IntersectionObserver at 15% visibility
motion.purpose: One-time section reveal as content scrolls into view; skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: header-typewriter
motion.purpose: Infinite type/delete loop cycling name, role and stack keywords beside the logo; frozen to a static value under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 40%, transparent); background: color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 10%, transparent); padding: 0.625rem 1.25rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #00d9ff; transition: all 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { border-color: #00d9ff; background: color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 20%, transparent); transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 0 40px color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 15%, transparent); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid #2a2a3f; background: transparent; padding: 0.625rem 1.25rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #9b9bb8; transition: all 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover, .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 40%, transparent); color: #f0f0ff; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Tappable filter pill; active state uses the same cyan-selected language as the rest of the system.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid #2a2a3f; padding: 0 0.875rem; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #9b9bb8; background: transparent; transition: color 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease, background 0.2s ease; } .ds-chip--active, .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #00d9ff; color: #00d9ff; background: color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 10%, transparent); }

components.name: Card Surface
components.description: Base container for project cards, stat tiles and skill groups.
components.html:
Stack principal

Angular / Laravel / PostgreSQL
components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 1rem; border: 1px solid #2a2a3f; background: color-mix(in srgb, #111118 80%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); padding: 1.5rem; } .ds-card-eyebrow { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #8888a8; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; color: #f0f0ff; margin: 0; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Header nav item; active route turns cyan, no underline or pill background.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #9b9bb8; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.2s ease; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: #f0f0ff; } .ds-nav-link--active { color: #00d9ff; }

components.name: Timeline Marker
components.description: Signature component: solid cyan dot marking each experience-timeline entry, on a hairline vertical rule.
components.css: .ds-timeline-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #00d9ff; box-shadow: 0 0 40px color-mix(in srgb, #00d9ff 15%, transparent); }

narrative.overview: This is a portfolio that wins trust through evidence, not decoration: every case study links to a real, live production system, and the interface around that content has to read as equally credible. The visual language is precise and sober — a near-black canvas, hairline borders instead of drop shadows, and a single accent color spent deliberately rather than everywhere. It should feel like a well-made engineering tool that happens to also be persuasive, never like a marketing template with a dark mode toggle. Two audiences read this site side by side — technical recruiters auditing stack depth, and non-technical business owners deciding whether to trust the person behind the code. The design stays legible and calm for both: no jargon-coded visual flourishes, just clean hierarchy, real content, and one confident accent color doing the pointing.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas by default; light theme is a deliberate alternate, not the "true" identity.
Flat surfaces at rest — elevation is borders and translucency, not shadow.
One accent (cyan) carries all primary interactive meaning; amber and violet are rare, deliberate seconds.
Two type families only: a distinctive display face for identity moments, a plain-spoken sans for everything read at length.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the only color that means "interactive" or "selected." Amber and violet never gain that responsibility.

rules.name: The AA Floor Rule
rules.body: Any text at body size or smaller must clear 4.5:1 contrast against its background. Muted Gray is for large/decorative text only.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Every piece of text is either Display (identity, rare) or Sans (everything else). A third family is a regression, not a refinement.

rules.name: The Glow-on-Response Rule
rules.body: Shadow only ever appears as a reaction to hover or focus, and it is always the cyan glow — never generic, never decorative, never present at rest.

dos: Do keep cyan as the singular primary/interactive accent; let amber and violet stay rare.
Do use a 1px hairline border (--color-border) as the default way to separate surfaces.
Do reserve --shadow-glow for hover/focus response only, never a resting decoration.
Do set body-length copy in IBM Plex Sans at 4.5:1+ contrast against its background.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animated or auto-playing element.
donts: Don't introduce a third type family.
Don't promote amber or violet into a primary-action or "selected" role.
Don't let muted/tertiary gray carry body-sized text.
